title: Coordinate-sign average and discrete derivative
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $q:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, and choose a coordinate $i\\in\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$. The uniform average of $x_iq(x)$ over the sign cube equals the uniform average of $\\bigl(q(x^{i,+})-q(x^{i,-})\\bigr)/2$, where $x^{i,+}$ and $x^{i,-}$ are obtained from $x$ by setting coordinate $i$ to $1$ and $-1$, respectively.
hypotheses_covered: $q$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
$i$ is a coordinate of the sign cube
